content.text:
Catalog search results now sort the way librarians file them, ignoring a leading "The", "A" or "An". "The Hobbit" now lists under H. All 60 tests pass.

The change is in `lib/catalog/search.js`. A small `filingTitle` helper strips the leading article, and the sort compares those filing titles. If two titles tie once the article is stripped, the full title decides, so the order is the same on every run.

Two edge cases I decided without asking you:
- **Title that is only an article:** "The" on its own is not stripped, so it still files as "The".
- **Words that merely start with an article:** "Anathem" and "Theory of Everything" are left alone, because the article has to be a whole word.

In `test/catalog.test.js` I changed the existing sort test, since "The Left Hand of Darkness" now sorts before "National Geographic". I also added a test that covers all the cases above.

I updated the stored description of `searchCatalog` in Kronomind, which still said "sorted by title".
